title: CrewAI — the org chart as code
intro: Roles in YAML, tasks in YAML, thin wiring in Python — and six projects that each add one capability.

steps.title: Three files
steps.body:
- **agents.yaml** — each agent is a *person*: role, goal, backstory, llm. The stock_picker crew: a trending-company finder ("always pick new companies — don't pick the same company twice"), a senior financial researcher, a stock picker.
- **tasks.yaml** — each task: description, expected_output, assigned agent; tasks chain.
- **crew.py** — the wiring: agents + tasks + **process** (sequential or hierarchical-with-manager), plus memory, tools, structured outputs.

steps.title: Six projects, one lesson each
steps.body: **debate** (two argue, one judges) → **financial_researcher** (search + report) → **stock_picker** (memory + push-notification tool) → **coder** (writes AND executes code) → **engineering_team** (a crew that builds working software: design, code, test roles).

points.label: Tools
points.note: Custom tools (the Pushover notification) attach to agents like SDK function tools.

points.label: Structure
points.note: Pydantic-typed task outputs — reports as objects, not prose.

points.label: Memory
points.note: stock_picker remembers past picks so 'never the same company twice' actually holds.

points.label: Hierarchy
points.note: A manager process delegates to workers — the org chart gains a boss.

steps.title: Templates make crews machines
steps.body:
`{sector}` in the YAML interpolates at kickoff — one crew definition, many runs. The crew is a **reusable machine with a personnel file**, not a script.

> [!tip] Backstories are prompt engineering wearing an HR badge — they steer tone, caution, and expertise more than most people expect.

steps.title: Where crews chafe
steps.body: Crews fit work that decomposes into **stable roles with clean hand-offs**. They chafe when you need precise control flow — retries, branches, checkpoints — which is exactly the gap the next week's explicit graphs fill.

recap:
**Model the org chart, not the algorithm.**

- agents.yaml (people) + tasks.yaml (work) + crew.py (process).
- Projects ladder: tools → structured outputs → memory → code execution → hierarchy.
- YAML templating turns a crew into a reusable machine.
- Need exact control flow? That's a graph, not a crew.
